extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, typesetters, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, copyediting, and typesetting manuscripts for publication—covering punctuation, capitalization, spelling, numerals, tables, spacing, and typographic conventions. Intended to be used by people producing or checking printed works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nouns: capitalization in titles of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Nouns: capitalization of, in titles of publications, 41
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal words in titles of publications should have capitalization applied as specified (see entry 41). Related guidance appears for combination nouns, plurals, and proper nouns elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered political divisions: capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbered political divisions, capitalization of names of
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize names of numbered political divisions according to the manual's rules (see entry for political divisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers: spelling and grouping rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers: commencing a sentence, to be spelled out, 96; consecutive, treatment of, 159, 173; in connected groups to be treated alike, 94; in groups of six or more closely connected, to be set in figures, 94; of less than three digits, to be spelled out in ordinary reading-matter, 94; round, treatment of, 95; use of comma after digits indicating thousands, 159; use of comma to separate, 154; use of dash for 'to' connecting, 173.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides when to spell numbers vs set in figures, consistent treatment in groups, punctuation between figures, and dash use for ranges. Consult referenced sections (94–96, 154, 159, 173) for examples and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals: spacing and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerals: Arabic, at beginning of lines and in headlines, spacing of, 271; Roman, at beginning of lines and in headlines, spacing of, 271; omission of period after, 124.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies spacing conventions for Arabic and Roman numerals in lines/headlines and when periods after numerals are omitted (see §§271 and 124).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission: punctuation and characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Omission: of comma after signatures, etc., 161; of figures in numbers or letters in middle of word, use of apostrophe for, 163; of period after headlines, etc., 125; after Roman numerals, 124; of 5, d, and th in dates, 102; of word or words, indicated by comma, 155; use of brackets for, 178; of ellipsis, 180.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists many cases where elements are omitted in typography and how omissions are indicated (apostrophe, brackets, ellipsis); see referenced sections for precise presentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open tables: headlines and setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Open tables: headlines for, 242; how to set, 241; specimen of, 250.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to set and head open-style tables, with specimens; see §§241–242, 250 for layout examples and box/head treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma before 'or' / 'nor' / 'and' in series
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences: of three or more links, use of comma before 'and,' 'or,' and 'nor' in, 143.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the serial (Oxford) comma policy: when a sequence has three or more items, guidance is provided about whether to include a comma before the final conjunction; see §143 for policy and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinals: capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinals: when capitalized, 13; when not, 45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives rules and exceptions for capitalizing ordinal words (see referenced sections for contexts and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers and offices: capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers: titles of, to be lower-cased, 21; of University of Chicago, to be capitalized, 49. Offices, capitalization of names of, 12, 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General policy: many official titles are lowercased in running text, but institutional/internal official titles (e.g., University of Chicago's organization) may be capitalized in official work; see §§12, 21, 49 for rules and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraphs: indention, quoted-paragraph first-lines, styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs: explained, 284; first lines of, in quoted prose matter to begin with quotation marks, 89; indention of, 274; styles of, 276 (cf. 284).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines paragraph forms (plain/regular), indentation conventions, and how quoted-paragraphs should begin (quotation marks on first lines); includes style variations and examples in §§274–276, 284.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and parenthetical clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Parentheses: rules for use of, 176-77; use of, for parenthetical clauses, 177 (cf. ISO, 167); in connection with figures or letters indicating subsections, 176; within parentheses, use of brackets for, 178. Parenthetical clauses: use of commas in connection with, 150; of dashes, 167, 169; of parentheses, 177 (cf.150,167).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives hierarchy for enclosing punctuation (parentheses vs brackets), punctuation around parenthetical clauses, and alternatives (commas, dashes). Refer to §§150, 167–177 for examples and when each device is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participial clauses: comma use
rubrics_metrics.description: Participial clauses, use of comma in connection with, 148.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for when participial modifiers require commas to avoid misreading; see §148 for restrictive vs nonrestrictive cases and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period (full stop): placement and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Period: placing of, in connection with quotation marks, 126; rules for use of, 122-26; to be omitted after abbreviations for linguistic epochs, 123; after headlines, 125; after initials of titles of publications, 123; after MS (=manuscript), 123; use of, after abbreviations, 123; at end of sentence, 122 (cf. 125); in classical references, 237, 239, note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive guidance on period placement relative to quotation marks, headlines, initials, and specialized references; see §§122–126 for systematic rules and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks: usage and punctuation placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation marks: not to be used in connection with reduced citations, 87; exception to this rule, 75; placing of colon in connection with, 136; of comma, 162; of ellipsis, 181; of exclamation point, 128; of interrogation point, 130; of period, 126; rules for use of, 74-91; to be omitted in references to Preface, Index, etc., 82; use of double and single, 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when to use or omit quotation marks (titles, reduced citations), and how other punctuation relates to quotation marks; includes single vs double quotation preferences and exceptions (see §§74–91, 136, 162, 181).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations: treatment and capitalization of first word
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations, how to treat, 74-91; first word of, lower-cased when connected with previous sentence, 57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains rules for block vs run-in quotations, shortened or reduced citations, and capitalization/punctuation of quotations when they continue or are integrated into sentence flow (see §57 and §74–91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per cent / Percent: numeric expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Per cent: to be expressed in figures, 94; not to be treated as an abbreviation, 123. Percentages: columns of, in tables, sometimes in distinctive type, 241.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy: express per cent values in figures (e.g., 5 percent), and treat 'percent' consistently (not as an abbreviation). Table columns of percentages may be set in distinctive type for clarity (see §241).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation: overall rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation: of extracts from modern authors, 112; rules for, 121-214.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive set of rules governing punctuation across contexts (quotations, citations, lists, parentheses, dashes, semicolons, etc.). See the indicated large section (121–214) for specifics and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation marks: typesetting and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation marks: omission of, in classical references, 237; placing of, with reference to indices in text, 232; to be printed in same type as word or letter preceding them, 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides typographic treatment of punctuation: when punctuation may be omitted in specialized references, how to place punctuation relative to footnote/reference indices, and the rule that punctuation should be set in the same type as the preceding character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicolon: use in enumerations and sentence division
rubrics_metrics.description: Semicolon: separating two or more distinct clauses in enumerations, 36; illustration of use of, compared with that of comma, 137; placing of, in connection with quotation marks, 140; rules for use of, 137-40; use of, in enumerations, 138; to mark division of sentence, 137; to separate passages in Scripture references containing chapters, 139.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains semicolon functions: separating complex list items, marking divisions within sentences, and its placement with quotation marks and references. See §§137–140 for examples distinguishing semicolons from commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series: comma before final conjunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Series, use of comma before final 'and,' 'or,' and 'nor' in, 143.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies policy on the serial comma (Oxford comma). See §143 for the manual's approach and contextual guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing: typographic spacing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing: in foundry type (and general) composition, 261-64; in linotype composition, 260; in monotype composition, 259; its effect on etymological divisions, 221; of divisional signs, 269; of figure columns in tables, 245; of formulae, 273; of headlines, 271; of metric symbols, 269; of monetary symbols, 270; of numerals at beginning of paragraphs, 271; of reading-matter in ruled tables, 246; of rules for setting of, 243; of short words, 268; rules for, 258-73; standard, 262; what is considered good, 262; with different sizes of spaces, samples of, 261.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive typographic spacing standards across composition systems, symbols, tables, short words, headlines, and formulas. Includes normative 'standard' spacing and examples of good practice. See §§258–273 for specifics and samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small caps: definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Small caps: defined, 257; how indicated, 257; use of, 52; in tabular work, 242, 249; in headings, 279.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines small caps, how to mark them in manuscripts, and where they should be used (headings, tables). See §257 and related sections for typographic examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelled out: words, phrases, and titles to spell out
rubrics_metrics.description: Spelled out, words, phrases, and titles which are to be, 92-105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists words, phrases, and kinds of titles that must be spelled out rather than abbreviated or set in figures; see §§92–105 for the enumerated items and examples (e.g., numbers at sentence starts, certain titles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling: rules and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Spelling: list of words of more than one, 119; of ages, 99; of books of Bible, 109; of centuries, 100; of Christian names, 93; of 'Company' and 'Brothers' in names of firms, 107; of decades, 101; of Egyptian dynasties, 100; of extracts from modern authors, 112; from Old English, 112; of indefinite article before h, u, etc., 114; of metric symbols, iii; of names of months, 102; of names of publications, 105; of names of regiments, 100; of numbers commencing a sentence, 96; of numbers of less than three digits, 94; of possessives of proper names ending in a sibilant, 113; of 'Railroad' and 'Railway,' 104; of round numbers, 95; of 'Saint,' 108; of sessions of Congress, 100; of states and territories, 106; of sums of money, 97; of time of day, 98; of titles, 92; of 'United States,' 103; of words denoting subsections, in literary references, no; rules for, 92-120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive orthographic rules covering many special word classes and contexts; consult the indicated subsections for exact spellings and exceptions in each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular work: setting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables: columns representing totals, percentages, etc., frequently set off by different type, 241; headlines of, how to set, 249; of two columns, to be set as open, 248; of more than two, as ruled, 248; open, headlines for columns in, 242; open, how to set, 241; ruled, box-heads for, 242; ruled, how to set, 241; rules for setting of, 241-50; rules for use of rules in, 243, 247; specimen, 250.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives complete guidance for open vs ruled tables, two-column vs multi-column formats, headline treatments, use of distinctive type for totals/percentages, and specimen tables showing correct layouts (see §§241–250).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles: capitalization and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles: academic, to be abbreviated, 22; civil and military, capitalization of, 21; honorary, 21; in direct address, 21; of nobility, 21; not capitalized when spelled out, 22; preceding names, to be spelled out, 92; list of exceptions, 92; 'vice,' 'ex-,' 'elect,' 'general,' and 'lieutenant,' constituting parts of, how to treat, 201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules determining when titles are capitalized or abbreviated, how compound-title elements are treated, and exceptions; specific treatment depends on position (preceding name, direct address) and institutional custom (see §§21–22, 92, 201).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of publications: capitalization and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of publications: capitalization of principal words in, 41; definite article not to be treated as part of, 43; to be italicized, 60; of subdivisions of, when to be roman-quoted, 82; use of capitals for various languages, 42; when to be spelled out, 105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies capitalization of principal words in titles, treatment of definite articles, italics vs roman-quote for different kinds of titles (books, articles, newspapers), and language-specific capitalization conventions (see §§41, 42, 60, 82, 105).

rubrics_metrics.name: References (legal and literary): abbreviations and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: References, legal, list of words and phrases used in, 61; literary: list of words to be abbreviated in, no (cf. 37, 54, 237); punctuation of, etc., 237, 239, note; use of dash in connection with, 174.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides word lists and punctuation conventions for constructing legal and literary references, including when to abbreviate and how to punctuate complex citations (see §§61, 174, 237–239).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthesis: period placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthesis: placing of period in connection with, 126.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives rule(s) for whether a period belongs inside or outside parentheses depending on whether the parenthetical material is a complete sentence or part of surrounding text (see §126).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentages in tables: distinctive type
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages: columns of, in tables, sometimes in distinctive type, 241.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested typographic treatment to set percentage columns apart (e.g., different type) for clarity; examples in table specimens (§241).

rubrics_metrics.name: Run-overs: avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Run-overs, avoidance of, 266.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typographic/layout guidance on avoiding unsightly line or line-group run-overs in page design; see §266 for specific measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman-quote: definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Roman-quote,' defined, 74, 253.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the use of roman (upright) type with quotation marks for certain shorter titles or citations as opposed to italics; see §74 and typographic terms §253 for how and when to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small words and divisions: hyphenation and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Short words: avoidance of divisions of, 216; spacing of, 268. Two-letter syllables, avoidance of, in divisions, 216.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance to avoid splitting short words or two-letter syllables across lines; spacing rules for short words to improve readability; see §§216, 268 for rules and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superscriptions and signatures: punctuation omission
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatures at end of letters or articles: omission of comma after, 161; of period, 125; rules for setting of, 50, 65. Superscriptions, omission of period after, 125-.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies punctuation and setting rules for signatures and superscriptions in correspondence and articles, including when to omit commas or periods (see §§50, 65, 125, 161).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreaders: hints and marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreaders: hints to, pp. 117-19; marks of, p. 123. Proofs, description of, 285-89.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides advice to proofreaders on common pitfalls, proofreading procedure, and standard proof-correction marks; also describes types of proofs and how proofs should be reviewed (see §§117–119, 123, 285–289).

rubrics_metrics.name: Point system and typographic units
rubrics_metrics.description: Point system, explanation of, 251-52. Unit, typographical, explained, 252; on monotype machine, 258. Sizes of type, in ordinary use, samples of, 252.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the typographic point system, units used in typesetting, sample sizes, and machine-specific considerations; important for page makeup and consistent type sizing (see §§251–258).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: rules for rules and box-heads
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules: double, use of, in tables, 247; rules for use of, in tables, 243. Box-heads for ruled tables, 242.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when and how to use rules (lines) in table design including double rules and box-head conventions; consult §§242–247 for layout patterns and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dashes: pause, transition, summing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pause, use of dash to indicate, 166. Transition, use of dash to indicate, 166. Summarizing clauses, use of dashes in connection with, 170.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the rhetorical/typographic functions of dashes—for indicating pauses, transitions, or summarizing clauses—and how to set and punctuate them; see §§166–170 for stylistic guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of measurement: abbreviations and case
rubrics_metrics.description: Units of measurement, abbreviations for, 111; spelled with lower-case initial letter, 55-.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies standard abbreviations for units and that unit abbreviations are spelled with lower-case initial letters, with spacing and punctuation conventions in the metric/measurement sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics vs roman-quote for titles and shorter works
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of works of art, plays, treatises, pamphlets, tracts, etc.: to be italicized or roman-quoted depending on type and length (multiple entries: e.g., pamphlets italicized 60; titles of shorter poems roman-quoted 81).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives systematic rules for when to italicize titles (books, pamphlets, treatises) and when to enclose in quotation marks/roman-quote (short poems, articles, shorter works). See the multiple title entries and §§60–82 for specific categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation placement with reference indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation marks: placing of, with reference to indices in text, 232; sequences of footnote indices, 232.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies whether punctuation should appear before or after footnote/reference superscripts and the correct sequencing and typography of multiple reference indices (see §232).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign names and particles ('van','von','de','le', etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Particles, in French, Dutch, and German names, capitalization of, 3. 'Van,' rule for treatment of, 3, 240. 'Von,' rule for treatment of, 3, 240.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives language-specific rules for capitalization and indexing of name particles (van, von, de, etc.), including how to alphabetize and present them in indexes (§3, 240).
